frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Closure/imperviousness of the aural channel — the ear sealed shut so that sound, and specifically the call (al-du'a'), does not penetrate or register. The residue is not "not-hearing" as a bare negation but a stopped-up, blocked receptive channel: the sealed state that makes aural reception impossible.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: Closure/imperviousness of the aural channel — the ear sealed shut so that sound, and specifically the call (al-du'a'), does not penetrate or register. The residue is not "not-hearing" as a bare negation but a stopped-up, blocked receptive channel: the sealed state that makes aural reception impossible.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every one of the 15 occurrences means "deaf / made deaf / became deaf." The shared root contribution across all of them is a BLOCKED HEARING CHANNEL — an ear stopped up so sound cannot get in. In 12 places it is the attribute/noun "the deaf" (as-summ, al-asamm, summan). Twice (5:71) it is the verb "they became deaf" (they closed their own ears). Once (47:23) it is causative "He made them deaf." The residue is stable and literal at the sensory level even when the reference is spiritual: disbelievers are likened to people whose ears are sealed to the call. Three times the object is explicitly al-du'a' (the call) — "the deaf do not hear the call" (21:45, 27:80, 30:52), which pins the residue to aural non-reception, not a general dullness.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: Form V sammu = fientive/reflexive entering the state ("became deaf / stopped their own ears," 5:71) — the voluntary self-closure is contributed by the pattern + agentive subject, not the root; Form IV asammahum = causative ("God made them deaf," 47:23) — the external causation is the pattern's; Form N (asamm/summ) = the resultant attribute/substantive. CONSTRUCTION: as-summ + al-du'a' (21:45, 27:80, 30:52) supplies "deaf TO the call"; the triad summ bukm 'umy (2:18, 2:171) and pairings with bukm (6:39, 8:22) / 'umy (17:97, 25:73, 43:40) supply the sensory-catalogue framing. CONTEXT: the near-universal reference to disbelievers/rejecters supplies the spiritual target. Subtracting all of these, the invariant root residue = sealed/blocked auditory receptivity.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 25:73 — "lam yakhirru 'alayha summan wa 'umyanan" ("they do not fall upon them [the ayat] deaf and blind") — here summ describes the manner in which believers do NOT receive revelation. The reference is inverted (a negated/desired non-state) and abstract, so one might argue the sensory core is bleached. But even here the residue holds: the contrast is precisely between an ear sealed to the ayat versus one open to them; "deaf" still contributes blocked aural reception. Likewise 5:71 sammu is fully metaphorical, yet the pattern still denotes entering the sealed-hearing state. Neither dissolves the residue.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Etymologically the broader Arabic core of s-m-m is "solid/sealed/stopped-up" (sakhra samma' = solid rock; a stoppered vessel), of which deafness is the ear-specific specialization. A competing framing would set the root residue at this more general "sealed/impervious/solid-shut" level rather than the narrower "aural closure." Within THIS corpus, however, that broader sense is never independently attested: all 15 occurrences are auditory. So the generic "sealed-solid" hypothesis is not falsifiable from the packet, and the narrowest contribution demonstrably present in every occurrence is the aural one. I adopt aural closure as the induced residue while noting the broader sense is compatible but not observable here.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinctive against its two nearest co-occurring roots: bukm (b-k-m, speech/tongue blocked — output) and 'umy ('-m-y, sight blocked — visual input). Smm is uniquely the AURAL input channel. It is also distinct from waqr (heaviness/dullness in the ear, partial) and from a generic "not understanding" (la ya'qilun, which appears alongside it in 8:22, 10:42, 2:171 as a separate consequence): summ is the channel being sealed, not the cognition failing. Residue is non-empty, distinctive, and falsifiable — a single occurrence using Smm for a non-auditory sealing/solidity, or for speech/sight blockage, would break it; none does.
internal_discovery.rationale: Universal presence holds across all 15 confirmed occurrences after subtracting form, construction, and context. The residue "sealed/blocked auditory receptivity" is present in every case: the 12 nominal forms name the bearer of that sealed state; the 2 Form V verbs denote entering it; the 1 Form IV verb denotes causing it. Three occurrences explicitly govern al-du'a' (the call), pinning the residue to aural non-reception; the recurrent triad/pairings with bukm and 'umy contrastively isolate Smm as the hearing-specific member. No occurrence resists — the only abstract/inverted cases (25:73, 5:71) still carry the sealed-ear contribution. Strength STRONG because coverage is complete, the contribution is invariant and construction-independent, and it is sharply distinctive against nearest roots. Not maximal only because the corpus never exhibits the broader etymological "sealed/solid" sense, so the induced residue is the narrow auditory specialization rather than a demonstrated general core — an honest boundary, not an inconsistency.

adversarial_verification.notes: Packet: 15/15 confirmed occurrences read (full coverage): 12 N, 2 V(I), 1 V(IV). CORE residue holds universally. Every occurrence denotes a sealed/impervious aural channel (deafness), not merely an event of not-hearing: the definite plural noun الصمّ names a fixed attributed class (10:42, 11:24, 43:40, 8:22, etc.); the Form IV causative فَأَصَمَّهُمْ (47:23) is an act of sealing the ears; Form I صَمُّوا (5:71x2) is entering the sealed state; and 21:45/27:80/30:52 show even a call failing to penetrate — direct support for imperviousness. So part (a) of the proposal (closure of hearing-reception) is demonstrably present in all 15 after subtracting form/construction/context; it is NOT refuted. DISTINCTIVENESS: strong — Smm is cleanly separable from its constant collocates سمع (the reception it negates, contrasted at 11:24 الاصم vs السميع), بكم (expressive/vocal channel), and عمي (visual channel); Smm is specifically the receptive aural channel sealed shut. FALSIFIABLE: yes; would fail on any non-aural sense (solid/hard) or a positive hearing sense — none occur in the packet. WHY NOT SUPPORTED: the contribution AS WORDED over-specifies by binding the residue to al-du'a' ('and specifically the call (al-du'a') does not penetrate or register'). The explicit call/du'a' element appears in only 4 occurrences (21:45, 27:80, 30:52, and 2:171 via دعاءً ونداءً). In the 11 listed failing occurrences there is no call/du'a' context at all (e.g., 2:18 'so they do not return'; 6:39 'in darkness'; 8:22 'who do not reason'; 17:97 physical resurrection state; 25:73 negated 'do not fall deaf/blind'; 5:71 spiritual/moral deafness coupled with blindness; 47:23 causative sealing). Under the packet's own rule to subtract context, al-du'a' is a context feature of the تُسْمِع-cluster, not root residue; its inclusion in the stated contribution is not demonstrable in those 11. Recommended tightening: residue = 'closure/imperviousness of the aural receptive channel — ear sealed shut so aural reception is impossible,' with al-du'a' demoted from residue to a cluster-specific context feature. With that correction the claim would be SUPPORTED; as literally worded it is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.
